tests.conclusion: not rejected: section counts are compatible with an even spread (p=0.8174)
not rejected: spacing is compatible with random placement (p=0.0728)

interpretation.reasoning: Humor is dense at the opening and in the letter, absent during the evening ride, and returns at the end with a punch line.
interpretation.plot_type_rationale: The event that sets the plot moving, the Bishop's demand, is itself delivered as a run of jokes, which suggests the complication is humorous. The final line is a punch line, so a punch-line plot is also plausible, but the ending does not appear to reinterpret the story as a whole.

plot_type_evidence.figure: 1 punch line at 0.99 of the text

central_complication.description: The Bishop orders Pumphrey, who never rides his bicycle, to acquire a conveyance by Easter.

evidence.figure: densest segment: one line every 29.3 words

central_complication.caveat: Attardo gives no formal definition of the central complication; this identification is intuitive.

pattern_findings.statement: Pumphrey is the most frequent target, appearing in about half of the humorous lines and across most of the story.
The evening ride contains no humorous lines at all, a serious-relief stretch between two humorous passages.
Jokes at the curate's expense are confined to the final fifth of the story.

evidence.figure: 4 lines, peripheral, from 0.80 to 0.99 of the text

pattern_findings.statement: Life-and-death oppositions recur from the letter to the last line.

readings.reading: The serious ride may work to make Pumphrey sympathetic before the comic resolution, so that the final joke lands on the curate rather than on him.
readings.caveat: This is a reading of the pattern, not something the counts establish.
